name: Fat grafting (lower eyelid / tear trough)

card.summary: Moving your own fat into the under-eye hollow to soften the tear trough: a real surgical option backed mostly by case series, with lumps and irregularities among the reported complications.
card.aka: Periorbital lipofilling, eyelid lipostructure, autologous fat transfer to the tear trough
card.note: Evidence is mainly case reports and retrospective series; contour irregularities and graft resorption are documented.

quick.overview:
Fat grafting for the lower eyelid takes a small amount of a person's own fat from another body area, processes it, and injects it into the hollow between the lower lid and cheek (the tear trough) to even out the contour. Forum users discuss it as a longer-lasting alternative to hyaluronic acid filler for under-eye hollows.

A systematic review of eyelid fat grafting found the literature consisted mostly of case reports and retrospective case series, so the quality of evidence is limited.
quick.mechanism: Harvested fat is injected as volume under the thin eyelid skin, filling the depression and smoothing the lid-cheek transition. Proponents also say the transferred tissue may improve skin quality, which is a claim researchers are still studying.
quick.risks: Reported problems with fat grafting in general include swelling, bruising, infection, lumpy or uneven contours, partial reabsorption of the fat and fat necrosis. The thin eyelid skin makes irregularities more visible. It is an operation performed by surgeons, and results can shift with major weight change.

lead: Fat grafting of the lower eyelid and tear trough, also called periorbital lipofilling or autologous fat transfer, is a surgical procedure in which a patient's own fat is harvested from another part of the body, processed and injected into the hollow beneath the lower eyelid to restore volume and smooth the transition to the cheek [2]. The look it aims for is a smoother, flatter line from lid to cheek, which people say makes the eyes look more rested and the midface fuller and younger [6][9].

It is used by people bothered by a pronounced tear trough, hollow under-eye contour or volume loss, and is sometimes combined with lower blepharoplasty or with fat repositioning [2][3][8]. In looksmaxxing communities it appears in discussions of hardmaxxing options for the eye area, alongside hyaluronic acid filler, infraorbital implants and eyelid surgery [4][10][11].

A 2016 systematic review of eyelid fat grafting covered 16 studies and 1,159 patients and reported satisfactory results with few complications, while noting wide variation in how fat is harvested, purified and reinjected and calling for long-term studies [1]. Much of the literature consists of case reports and retrospective case series [1].
infobox: Lower eyelid, tear trough, sometimes upper eyelid and cheek
Areas with spare fat such as abdomen or thighs [2]

paras: Fat transfer is done in stages: fat is harvested, processed, and injected in small amounts into the target area [2]. Around the eyes it is used to improve lower-eyelid contour and make up for volume loss [2].

Facial rejuvenation has shifted in recent decades from removing tissue toward restoring volume, often combined with repositioning of tissue [2]. Fat grafting and transconjunctival fat repositioning are both used for the tear trough, and the two can be combined in a single operation [3].

The tear trough is the groove running from the inner corner of the eye down and outward across the lid-cheek junction. A 2012 review in Aesthetic Surgery Journal by Stutman and Codner covers its anatomy, grading systems and treatments, including hyaluronic acid filler, fat grafting, skeletal implants and fat transposition [7]. A 2013 review of the science of facial aging describes age-related changes to the facial skeleton, soft tissue, muscle and skin that contribute to hollowing [12].

Facial rejuvenation has moved over recent decades from removing tissue toward restoring volume, and lower-lid hollowness can come from fat loss, bony recession of the orbit rim or ligament tethering, among other causes [2][7][12]. In looksmaxxing discussion, a recessed infraorbital rim is a common explanation members give for under-eye hollows and a tired look, and they weigh fat grafting against implants and filler [11].

Fat transfer is done in stages: harvest, processing and injection of small amounts into the target area [2]. Variants described in the literature include microfat and nanofat preparations, fluid fat injections, and stromal vascular fraction (SVF) gel. A retrospective review of 98 consecutive patients treated with superficial enhanced fluid fat injection (SEFFI) reported using a finer preparation for the eyelids and tear trough, good or excellent results in all patients at about six months, and oil cysts in three patients [13]. A review of SVF gel, a centrifuged fat-derived product, describes its use alone or with transconjunctival eyebag removal for tear trough deformity, with high satisfaction and fairly low complication rates reported by its authors [14].

Fat can also be combined with surgical approaches. In a 54-patient case series, Wong and Mendelson used an extended transconjunctival lower-lid approach in which orbital fat was redistributed under a released tear trough ligament; they reported a 2 percent revision rate and no chemosis or lid retraction over a mean 10 months follow-up [8]. Fat grafting and transconjunctival fat repositioning are both used for the tear trough and can be performed in one operation [3]. Wikipedia also describes newer stem-cell-enriched grafts and nanografts that contain no adipose cells but retain stem-cell content [2].

A systematic review published in 2016 in the Journal of Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery examined indications, technique and complications of eyelid fat grafting, covering 16 studies and 1,159 patients; the authors described results as satisfactory with few complications and noted heterogeneity in technique [1].

Individual series include the SEFFI review of 98 patients with about six months' follow-up [13] and the 54-patient extended transconjunctival series with fat redistribution [8]. Reviews of SVF gel describe favourable satisfaction but give no controlled comparison [14]. A systematic review of treatments for periorbital hyperpigmentation, a related under-eye concern, addresses pigment and structural causes of dark circles [17].

A registered retrospective follow-up study (n=120) looked at lower-eyelid melanin and wrinkles after blepharoplasty for lower-eyelid bags, which is related but concerns blepharoplasty rather than fat grafting itself [5]. A registered phase 1/2 trial of autologous stromal vascular fraction for skin regeneration has also been listed [6]. No randomized trial comparing fat grafting with hyaluronic acid filler in the tear trough has been published.

Hyaluronic acid filler is a non-surgical route to tear trough volume; a 2024 review of filler adverse effects covers nodules, granuloma and migration across filler treatments generally [15]. In a looksmax.org thread, a poster with recessed infraorbital areas weighs infraorbital implants, fat grafting and filler: implants are described as most definitive but costly with downtime, fat grafting as less predictable than filler and not reversible, and filler as quick with worries about migration near the eye [11].

Another thread discusses whether fat grafting can be placed over infraorbital implants, with a reply saying it can be done and that infection risk exists but is not high [16]. These are forum accounts, not controlled comparisons. No randomized trial comparing fat grafting with hyaluronic acid filler in the tear trough has been published.

Complications listed for fat transfer in general include swelling, bruising, hematoma, infection, hypertrophic scarring at the donor site, contour irregularities and injury to underlying structures from the cannula [2]. The body may reabsorb a portion of grafted fat, and fat necrosis is a recognized risk [2]. Large weight gain or loss can alter the result because transferred fat behaves like fat elsewhere in the body [2].
The systematic review of eyelid fat grafting specifically addressed complication rates, reflecting that the thin periorbital tissue is a sensitive site [1].

The 2016 review reported few complications overall, and the SEFFI series reported oil cysts in 3 of 98 patients [1][13]. Forum users note that fat grafting is not as predictable as filler and cannot be reversed, and raise worries about looking puffy or bloated if too much volume is placed in the lid [11]. Wikipedia reports that the body may reabsorb a portion of grafted fat, which is why surgeons often describe a staged approach [2].

Users on looksmax.org post before-and-after results of eyelid fat grafting. In one thread about an upper-eyelid result, the poster described a very positive experience, while a reply said fat grafting can address visible hollowing but that an underlying ptosis problem is often also present, so it may treat symptoms rather than causes [4]. Another reply described searching for a surgeon abroad who publishes real before-and-after photos [4].

Eye-area discussion on the forum often centres on lower eyelid support, infraorbital rim projection and eyelid shape as parts of overall eye appearance. Posters weigh fat grafting against implants, filler and eyelid retraction surgery depending on cost, downtime and whether the hollow is soft-tissue or bony [11][16].

timeline.event: Stutman and Codner review tear trough anatomy and treatment options including fat grafting, filler, implants and fat transposition [7].
Review of the science and theory of facial aging describes the tissue changes behind midface hollowing [12].
Retrospective review of 98 patients treated with superficial enhanced fluid fat injection for facial and periocular volume defects [13].
Systematic review of eyelid fat grafting covers 16 studies and 1,159 patients [1].
Wong and Mendelson report extended transconjunctival blepharoplasty with tear trough ligament release and fat redistribution in 54 patients [8].
Review of SVF gel fat grafting for facial rejuvenation, including tear trough deformity [14].
Review of dermal filler adverse effects including nodules, granuloma and migration [15].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, eyelid fat grafting is discussed as a surgical route to fuller upper and lower eyelids, with surgeon selection and visible before-and-after results a recurring concern [4].

claims.claim: Fat grafting can fix hollow eyelids and make the eye area look better.
claims.believers: Users share photos of upper-eyelid results and describe them as strong improvements, treating the procedure as a major positive for the eye area [4].
claims.experts: The only systematic review located describes the evidence as mostly case reports and retrospective case series, so outcomes and satisfaction rates across techniques are not established by controlled trials [1].

claims.claim: Fat grafting may only treat symptoms if there is an underlying ptosis problem.
claims.believers: One forum reply says fat grafting is good for severe upper-eyelid hollowing but that ptosis is often present underneath, so the graft alone does not correct the cause [4].
claims.experts: No controlled studies compare fat grafting with ptosis surgery for this situation.

claims.claim: Fat grafting lasts much longer than filler because the transferred fat becomes living tissue.
claims.believers: Forum users say a graft that takes a blood supply can stay for years, which makes it attractive compared with filler that needs repeating [11].
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports that part of transferred fat is reabsorbed, and the 2016 systematic review called for long-term studies of outcomes [1][2].

claims.claim: Filler under the eyes migrates or causes a puffy look, so fat or implants are safer.
claims.believers: One poster worries filler near the eye is prone to migrate and cause a bloated look, but values its fast recovery [11].
claims.experts: A 2024 review of filler adverse effects covers nodules, granuloma and migration, and reports on management; it does not compare against fat grafting [15].

claims.claim: Fat grafting can be placed over infraorbital implants.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org reply says it can be done, with a small infection risk, higher with silicone because of the capsule [16].
claims.experts: No controlled studies address fat grafting over implants.

claims.claim: Fat grafting can improve skin quality as well as volume.
claims.believers: Proponents of stem-cell and SVF preparations say the tissue can improve skin around the eyes [2][14].
claims.experts: A registered phase 1/2 trial of stromal vascular fraction for skin regeneration is listed, and reviews describe satisfaction but limited controlled data [6][14].

angle.text: Fat grafting fills a hollow under the eye with the person's own tissue, which proponents say gives a smoother contour and a more rested look that lasts longer than many fillers. Surgeons sometimes pair it with eyelid surgery or midface work.
